question: Do the exact right-hand conjectures in Erdos683.erdos_683 and Erdos961.erdos_961 express equivalent mathematical assertions?

evidence.observation: Session 9 requires both complete files and forbids promoting the TODO without an exact two-directional map.

P n k is the largest prime factor of Nat.choose n k. The conjecture asserts one fixed real c>0 and, for every 0<k<n, P n k > min (n-k+1) (k^(1+c)). Its only equivalence assertion is the unproved comment `TODO: Erdos 683 and 961 are equivalent.`

Erdos961Prop K L says every interval Set.Ico m (m+L), for m≥K+1, contains an integer having a prime factor greater than K. The noncomputable f K is the least such L for K>0. The main conjecture asserts ∃C:ℕ, eventually f K < (Real.log K)^C.

For r≤N and a threshold T≥r, primes q>T cannot divide r!, so q divides choose N r exactly when q divides some numerator integer in [N-r+1,N]. Thus the relevant bridge is P N r>T ↔ the length-r interval starting at N-r+1 contains a non-(T+1)-smooth integer, subject to the stated range conditions.

On the branch N-r+1>r^(1+c), Erdos 683 supplies such an interval prime with T=r^(1+c). Reparameterizing gives only f(T)≤ceil(T^(1/(1+c))) up to rounding and sufficiently large range conditions—a fixed power bound. Erdos 961 instead requires the much stronger polylogarithmic bound f(T)<(log T)^C. No choice of fixed c converts the former into the latter.

limitations: This does not prove that the two open number-theoretic propositions have different truth values; it establishes that the exact sources do not provide the claimed equivalence and that the natural bridge yields mismatched quantitative strengths.
